messages:
Ava: heads up — rolling a v2.2-int8-mp canary (5% traffic) for prod-candidates. objective: cut cost ~18% with mixed-precision int8 paths.
Raj: nice. any heavy-query cohorts we should watch? long-code, kb-sysdocs, and conversational followups.
Ava: focusing on kb-sysdocs and multi-turn followups. initial telemetry looks fine but qa-bot fired a hallucination alert on the kb slice.
qa-bot: ALERT: hallucination_rate(kb-sysdocs) increased from 2.1% -> 3.9% (+1.8% absolute) over 10m window. source: sim-eval/1751239999.
Nina: that's a pretty big jump. what metric exactly is this alert using?
qa-bot: metric=P_incorrect_fact (auto-labeled via entity-checker), window=10m, min-traffic=2000 reqs.
Diego: is this relative or absolute threshold crossing? our roll gate is typically absolute >1% for 15m OR relative >20% for 10m, right?
Sophia: documented guardrail: absolute increase >1.0% sustained for 20m triggers canary hold; autofallback configured for absolute >1.5% for 10m. but infra sometimes has 10m windows.
Ava: current burst is +1.8% over 10m so autofallback could fire soon if sustained. I've paused any further ramp and dropped traffic to 2%.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy v2.2-int8-mp -> initial 5% at 1751239950. traffic reduced to 2% at 1751240020 by Ava. monitor: https://ops/redwood/canary/1751239999
Raj: good call. Nina, can you run the seeded offline hallucination eval (perturbed prompts) against v2.2 and baseline v2.0 to see whether the delta holds?
Nina: starting eval job `eval-hall-1751239999` now. will include prompt-perturbation + fact-check harness. ETA 14m.
Diego: also check KB grounding hits (exact match to KB entries). quantization can subtly change tokenization/normalization upstream and hurt lookup heuristics.
Ava: I pulled KB hit-rate: baseline 85.2% -> v2.2 83.5% (-1.7%). matches upward hallucination delta.
Sophia: interesting. could be embedding upstream shift or tokenization whitespace behavior. Was tokenizer stable between builds?
Ava: tokenizer same. compiler emitted different kernel path for RMS-norm in int8 path (fast-rms-v2). suspect numerical drift.
Raj: mitigation options: 1) revert to float16 RMS kernel for kb-heavy requests; 2) enable soft-routing: route kb-sysdocs queries to baseline v2.0; 3) tune quant calibration (per-channel).
Nina: testing a quick ablation: run v2.2 with rms_fallback=true (force f16 kernel) in shadow for 20m.
Diego: if rms_fallback fixes KB hit-rate, we should add that as a temporary canary override and also file fix in runtime kernel selection.
Ava: added ticket M-4810 for kernel variance. Tagging as P0 for model-onboard quality.
qa-bot: NOTE: apply smoothing to alerts: 10m moving average + 3-sample median to reduce flapping.
Sophia: agree on smoothing. but we must not mask real regressions. keep autofallback thresholds but apply debounce: require 2 consecutive windows before auto-action.
Raj: policy update proposal: autofallback triggers if (absolute_inc >= 1.5% && sustained >=10m) OR (absolute_inc >=1.0% && sustained >=20m). AND require 2 consecutive evaluation windows to actuate.
Ava: sounds reasonable. I'll circulate for approval in eng-ml. For now, keep canary at 2% until nina's eval completes.
Nina: eval done: seeded results show P_incorrect_fact: baseline 2.12% -> v2.2 3.85% (replicated across 3 seeds). RMS-fallback replica reduces v2.2 to 2.25%.
Diego: RMS-fallback looks promising. can we flip runtime flag for the canary traffic only?
Ava: yes, we can set runtime override `runtime.rms_kernel=fp16` for the v2.2 shard. prepping change.
deploy-bot: staged config update prepared. will apply to canary shard on confirmation.
Raj: one more ask: log logits/embedding diffs for kb-sysdocs L1 tokens for the failing cases and add to M-4810. want to see per-token drift.
Ava: done, attached diffs to ticket. quick sample shows embedding norms shifted by ~0.04 on first KB-token.
Sophia: good triage. if RMS-fallback keeps metrics within +/-0.3% of baseline for 30m, we can resume ramp with a guard: enable soft-routing to baseline for any KB queries until kernel fix lands.
Nina: running 30m RMS-fallback shadow run now. will report.
Diego: thanks team. also schedule kernel regression unit test in CI for RMS numeric parity across quant paths.
Ava: will push a CI job. summary: halted ramp, throttle=2%, ran evaluations, identified RMS kernel numeric drift as likely cause, RMS-fallback fixes in shadow, created M-4810. next: decide on temporary runtime override vs rollback.
Sophia: thanks all. keep eng-ml & incidents updated. :thumbsup:
